main_issue: Whether alcohol will be served at the Saturday housewarming in the shared flat (D objects), and who bears the cost of the already-bought drinks

A-B.evidence: B agrees on getting soft drinks (T2, T4), worries about boss expecting drinks (T7); A cites B's boss in T14, T16 — both want to keep alcohol.

A-C.evidence: C says A and B should cover the drinks cost themselves (T10); A stresses having spent $150 from the fund and unreturnable (T9, T14), not accepting.

A-D.evidence: D proposes a non-alcoholic party with drinks elsewhere (T15); A rejects: 'doesn't really solve the problem' (T16).

B-C.evidence: C says A and B should pay for the drinks (T10), while B wants alcohol for his boss (T7); B never responds on money.

B-D.evidence: B says D's objection is 'a problem' because he told guests there would be drinks (T7); D's no-alcohol stance (T13, T15) stands; no direct exchange.

C-D.evidence: C backs fairness for D's money (T10); D says it's not about money (T11, T13); C insists money must be sorted (T12) and never addresses D's no-alcohol request.
